Scope: 44 ready-built factories of 900 m² each in 11 blocks (B1–B11), with external utilities, roads, parking and street lighting.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours (225,761 man-hours in total). At the 10-Nov-2026 data date the project is 83.5% complete against 81.9% planned, 1.6% ahead. This week added 2.2% against 1.4% planned. Construction is now 0.2% ahead of its plan, but Blocks B4 and B5 are still about 18% behind theirs.

Ahead of plan, and the forecast finish moved a week earlier. The P6 update now finishes the project on 24-Feb-2027, ten days before the contract completion date of 06-Mar-2027, still with zero float on project completion. All 74 activities in progress are counted as behind schedule and 221 activities have missed their start. The civil works milestone slipped three more days in P6, to 01-Dec-2026, and the milestone for site levelling, local roads and parking has still not started.

The weekly report and the P6 update use different baselines for the discipline milestones. For civil works the weekly report's baseline is 21-Feb-2027, while the P6 baseline is 01-Oct-2026 and the P6 forecast is now 01-Dec-2026, 61 days after its own baseline and three days later than last week. Mechanical works slipped four days to 31-Dec-2026. Electrical and architectural works moved three days earlier to 30-Jan-2027, 40 days after their P6 baseline of 21-Dec-2026, and construction completion moved eight days earlier to 15-Feb-2027. The contractual milestone for site levelling, local roads and parking (P6 baseline 12-Feb-2026) has still not started and is again forecast for the data date itself.

Data notes

  • The weekly report workbook (WPR #38, .xlsb) has no text version in MD Files, so its figures were read from the original workbook in All Files. This week's values are the change from WPR #37 (03-Nov-2026, in the W06 folder).
  • The workbook's weekly columns were not updated: they repeat last week's 3,317 planned and 3,606 earned man-hours (construction 2,964 and 3,015, Block B1 104), while the to-date totals rose by 3,104 planned and 4,877 earned. The to-date change is used here.
  • The block rows add up to 103,702 earned man-hours against a construction total of 113,042; the gap of 9,340 is consistent with Block B6 being under-recorded (437 of 11,824 man-hours, against 97.8% planned), unchanged for a third week.
  • Testing and commissioning is recorded at 42.4% earned against 13.6% planned, while the Testing sheet, unchanged this week, shows mechanical testing 8% complete and electrical and fire testing not started.
  • The report page's headline plan and earned values, the Risk & Issue log and the 05-Nov-2026 presentation's planned and actual progress are cost-based; the log and the presentation label this cost-based figure as actual progress. This report uses the physical (man-hour) figures only.
  • The weekly report's general information still gives a forecast completion of 06-Mar-2027 (no variance), while its milestone sheet and the P6 update give 24-Feb-2027. Its milestone baselines also differ from the P6 baseline (for example civil works 21-Feb-2027 against 01-Oct-2026).
  • Procurement: the weekly report counts all 83 materials delivered (completed 13-Oct-2026), while the 05-Nov-2026 presentation lists five key items not fully delivered.
  • FIRs issued fell from 999 last week to 982 this week (980 closed, 2 pending); the 05-Nov-2026 presentation still shows 999 / 969 / 30. Shop drawings: 158 in the weekly report, 157 in the presentation.
  • Invoice log: the penalties of 2,000 and 1,000 on invoices 4 and 5 are added to their net values instead of deducted, so the net total reads 45,048,303 and the total deduction falls by 3,000; the paid amount also rose by 3,000 to 37,079,227.
  • The November manpower and equipment actuals (22 staff, 267 labourers, 20 items of equipment) repeat October's figures, against 343 workers and 37 items of equipment by day in the presentation. The safety sheet gives 16,440 man-hours this week for the third week running.
  • The P6 file's project code is still DAM3-02-3 with a planned start of 14-Mar-2023, and the procurement sheets carry project ID DAM-05-009. The invoice summary still shows 0 submitted invoices although seven are listed.
  • The Risk & Issue log names Engr Hamdi as MODON PM; the weekly report names Engr. Affat Al-Enezi. Its dashboard shows 244 open risks and 128 open issues, against 5 open risks and no open issues in the logs.
  • No photo files and no P6 PDF layout were uploaded this week; the photos are taken from the presentation and P6 dates come from the XER file.
